title.en: The amazing world of solutes, solvents and solutions

text.en: Every sip of homemade ORS tastes the same, no matter how much you drink. Why is it uniform?

A uniform mixture of two or more substances is called a solution.
When a solid dissolves in a liquid, the solid is the solute and the liquid is the solvent.
In sugar water, sugar is the solute and water is the solvent, and water is called the universal solvent because it dissolves many substances.
A solution looks the same throughout, particles do not settle, and cannot be separated by filtering.
Solubility is the amount of solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent at a given temperature.
A solution that cannot dissolve any more solute at that temperature is saturated, otherwise it is unsaturated.
Heating usually increases the solubility of solids, so more sugar dissolves in hot water than in cold.
Gases are less soluble at higher temperature, which is why fish need oxygen dissolved in cool water.
Stirring and crushing the solute speed up dissolving but do not change how much dissolves.
Solutions are everywhere: lemonade, sea water, ORS and air, and some mixtures like chalk in water are suspensions, not solutions.

problem.en: In a salt solution, name the solute, solvent and solution.

prompt.en: Why can we not filter sugar from sugar water?

requiredIdeas.en: They are dissolved and spread evenly.
So they pass through the filter.

points.en: Solute dissolves in solvent to form a solution.
Saturated solutions cannot dissolve more solute.
